result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Multiple Imputation with mice" subtitle: "Chained equations · pmm · m imputations · convergence · checking · pooling with Rubin's rules · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 2: simple methods are biased or have wrong SEs - Today: **multiple imputation (MI)** with the **`mice`** package - By the end you can: - run `mice()` and read its **methods and predictor matrix** - **check** convergence and imputed values - **analyse** each data set and **pool** with Rubin's rules ::: # Topic 1 — The idea {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Three steps ::: {.eq} **Impute** (m times) → **Analyse** (each data set) → **Pool** (Rubin's rules) ::: ::: {.incremental} 1. Create **m complete data sets**; the imputed values **differ** between them, reflecting **uncertainty** 2. Run the **same analysis** in each (`with()`) 3. **Pool**: the estimate is the **average**; the variance combines **within-imputation** and **between-imputation** variance (`pool()`) - `mice` uses **chained equations**: each incomplete variable is imputed from a model with **all the other variables**, cycling through them (**iterations**) ::: ## Setup before imputing ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ini <- mice(dat, maxit = 0, printFlag = FALSE) ini$method ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` age sex education bmi smoker activity sbp hba1c "" "" "" "pmm" "pmm" "pmm" "pmm" "pmm" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **pmm** (predictive mean matching): the missing value is replaced by an **observed value from an adult with a similar prediction**; keeps the **distribution** and works for skewed variables - Binary variables: make them **factors** and `mice` uses **logistic regression** (`logreg`) - The **predictor matrix** (1 = use as predictor): by default **everything predicts everything**; remove the **id**, include the **outcome** (SBP) ::: ## Run it ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat2 <- dat |> mutate(smoker = factor(smoker, labels = c("No", "Yes"))) imp <- mice(dat2, m = 20, maxit = 10, seed = 2038, printFlag = FALSE) imp$method ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` age sex education bmi smoker activity sbp hba1c "" "" "" "pmm" "logreg" "pmm" "pmm" "pmm" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **20 imputations**, **10 iterations**, a **fixed seed** (reproducible). Smoking is now imputed by `logreg`, the continuous variables by `pmm`. ::: # Topic 2 — Checking {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Convergence ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(imp, c("bmi", "hba1c", "activity")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_multiple_imputation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Mean and SD of the imputed values **by iteration**, one line per imputation - Lines should **mix** (cross freely) with **no trend** - A trend or lines that **stay apart** = not converged: more iterations or fix the model ::: ## Imputed vs observed values ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} densityplot(imp, ~ bmi) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_multiple_imputation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} **Blue** = observed, **red** = imputed (each imputation). Imputed BMI is **shifted to the right** (mean 25.1 vs 24.1 observed): adults with a **high SBP**, who are more often missing, tend to have a **higher BMI**. Differences are **allowed** when the missingness is not random; **implausible values** are not. ::: # Topic 3 — Analyse and pool {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## with() and pool() ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity)) pooled <- pool(fit) summary(pooled, conf.int = TRUE)[, c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "df", "conf.low", "conf.high")] |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` term estimate std.error df conf.low conf.high 1 (Intercept) 85.437 1.955 258.151 81.586 89.287 2 age 0.413 0.020 1234.023 0.374 0.452 3 sexMale 2.998 0.537 801.835 1.944 4.053 4 bmi 0.790 0.066 243.317 0.661 0.920 5 smokerYes 1.965 0.668 281.399 0.649 3.281 6 activity -0.490 0.096 592.055 -0.679 -0.301 ``` ::: ::: ## Comparison with complete case ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_cc <- lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity, data = dat) s <- summary(pooled, conf.int = TRUE) round(rbind(complete_case = summary(m_cc)$coefficients["bmi", 1:2], multiple_imputation = unlist(s[s$term == "bmi", c("estimate", "std.error")])), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error complete_case 0.685 0.071 multiple_imputation 0.790 0.066 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **MI 0.79 (SE 0.066)** against **complete case 0.69 (SE 0.071)**; the truth is about **0.80 to 0.86**. MI **removes most of the bias** and is **more precise** because it **uses all 2,000 adults**. The SE is **honest**: it includes the **between-imputation** variance. ::: ## Rules for good imputation models ::: {.good} 1. Include **all variables in the analysis model**, **including the outcome** 2. Include **auxiliary variables** that predict the missing values or the missingness 3. Include **interactions** and **non-linear terms** you will analyse (Session 4) 4. Use **enough imputations** (Session 4); set a **seed** 5. **Check** convergence and imputed values ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `missing-workshop/labs/lab3_mice.R` - default methods and predictor matrix - `mice()` with 20 imputations, convergence, densities - `with()` and `pool()`, comparison with complete case ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ral47h.yal6o7" data-show="SXQgaW1wdXRlcyBieSBib3Jyb3dpbmcgYW4gb2JzZXJ2ZWQgdmFsdWUgZnJvbSBhbiBhZHVs dCB3aXRoIGEgc2ltaWxhciBwcmVkaWN0aW9u" data-explain="cG1tIHByZWRpY3RzIGEgdmFsdWUgZm9yIGVhY2ggbWlzc2luZyBlbnRyeSwgZmluZHMgb2Jz ZXJ2ZWQgYWR1bHRzIHdpdGggY2xvc2UgcHJlZGljdGlvbnMsIGFuZCB0YWtlcyBvbmUgb2Yg dGhlaXIgYWN0dWFsIHZhbHVlcywgc28gaW1wdXRhdGlvbnMgbG9vayBsaWtlIHJlYWwgZGF0 YS4="} What does predictive mean matching (pmm) do? - It imputes the mean of the observed values in each imputed data set - It predicts the missing value from a regression and uses the prediction as it is - It matches adults with missing values to adults with the same pattern of missingness - It imputes by borrowing an observed value from an adult with a similar prediction ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ralhg3.yall5h" data-show="VG8gcmVmbGVjdCB0aGUgdW5jZXJ0YWludHkgYWJvdXQgdGhlIG1pc3NpbmcgdmFsdWVzIGlu IHRoZSBwb29sZWQgU0Vz" data-explain="VGhlIGltcHV0ZWQgdmFsdWVzIGRpZmZlciBiZXR3ZWVuIGRhdGEgc2V0cywgYW5kIHNvIGRv IHRoZSBlc3RpbWF0ZXMuIFRoZSBiZXR3ZWVuLWltcHV0YXRpb24gdmFyaWFuY2UgY2Fycmll cyB0aGUgdW5jZXJ0YWludHkgZHVlIHRvIG1pc3NpbmcgZGF0YS4="} Why are m imputed data sets created and analysed separately? - To reflect the uncertainty about the missing values in the pooled SEs - To obtain m independent estimates that are averaged without further steps - Because each variable needs its own completed data set to be analysed - To check that the results are identical across the m data sets of adults ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="raluou.yalzmw" data-show="VGhleSBhdmVyYWdlIHRoZSBlc3RpbWF0ZXMgYW5kIGFkZCB1cCB0d28gc291cmNlcyBvZiB2 YXJpYW5jZQ==" data-explain="VGhlIHBvb2xlZCBlc3RpbWF0ZSBpcyB0aGUgbWVhbiBvZiB0aGUgbSBlc3RpbWF0ZXMsIGFu ZCB0aGUgdG90YWwgdmFyaWFuY2UgaXMgdGhlIG1lYW4gd2l0aGluLWltcHV0YXRpb24gdmFy aWFuY2UgcGx1cyBhbiBpbmZsYXRlZCBiZXR3ZWVuLWltcHV0YXRpb24gdmFyaWFuY2Uu"} What do Rubin's rules do? - They select the best imputed data set by the model fit statistics - They average the imputed data sets before the model is fitted to them - They average the estimates and add up two sources of variance - They correct the p-values for the number of variables with missing data ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ram7xi.yame48" data-show="VGhlIGl0ZXJhdGlvbnMgaGF2ZSBtaXhlZCB3ZWxsLCBzbyBpdCBoYXMgcHJvYmFibHkgY29u dmVyZ2Vk" data-explain="TWl4aW5nIHdpdGhvdXQgYSB0cmVuZCBpcyB0aGUgc2lnbiBvZiBjb252ZXJnZW5jZS4gSXQg ZG9lcyBub3QgcHJvdmUgdGhhdCB0aGUgaW1wdXRhdGlvbiBtb2RlbCBpcyByaWdodCwgd2hp Y2ggbmVlZHMgY2hlY2tzIG9mIHRoZSBpbXB1dGVkIHZhbHVlcy4="} In the convergence plot the lines of different imputations cross freely, with no trend. What does this suggest? - The imputed values are the same in all of the data sets generated - The iterations have mixed well, so it has probably converged - The imputation model is correct and no other check is needed at all - The number of iterations is too small and has to be increased ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="raml68.yamslm" data-show="QSB1bmlxdWUgY29kZSBjYXJyaWVzIG5vIGluZm9ybWF0aW9uLCBhbmQgYXMgYSBwcmVkaWN0 b3IgaXQgYWRkcyBub2lzZQ==" data-explain="QSB1bmlxdWUgaWRlbnRpZmllciBoYXMgbm8gcmVsYXRpb25zaGlwIHdpdGggdGhlIHZhcmlh YmxlcywgYnV0IHdvdWxkIGJlIHRyZWF0ZWQgYXMgYSBwcmVkaWN0b3IsIHdoaWNoIGFkZHMg bm9pc2UgYW5kIGNhbiBjYXVzZSBlcnJvcnMu"} Why is the id column left out of the imputation model? - mice cannot read character variables when they are stored in the data frame - The id is nearly always strongly correlated with the outcome variable in the data - A unique code carries no information, and as a predictor it adds noise - Variables without missing values are not allowed in the imputation model ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Impute → analyse → pool** (`mice`, `with`, `pool`) - **pmm** for continuous, **factors** for binary (`logreg`) - Include the **outcome** and **auxiliary** variables; drop the **id** - **Check**: convergence plot, density of imputed vs observed - MI **0.79** vs complete-case **0.69** (truth about 0.80) ::: **Next:** Session 4: diagnostics, derived variables and the number of imputations

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
